problem: VLN agents pre-trained on limited simulator environments or on web images concatenated into path-instruction pairs see unreasonable room layouts and ambiguous or random actions. This limits their generalization to unseen environments and their layout reasoning.
motivation: Massive YouTube house-tour videos offer diverse real environments, real room layouts and native navigation actions, but they had not been used for VLN. Turning these raw unlabeled videos into VLN-like path-instruction pairs could provide in-domain pre-training data and layout knowledge.
key_idea: Build YouTube-VLN by grouping video frames into room nodes, choosing the min-entropy frame per node, and filling instruction templates with pseudo-labeled actions, then pre-train with a trajectory judgment task that discriminates real from shuffled trajectories to learn layout reasoning.
insight: Ablations show each element adds gains: reasonable ordered trajectories (+1.27 SR val-unseen over shuffled), pseudo-labeled actions (+1.10 SR), and trajectory judgment (+2.05 SR val-seen, +0.60 SR val-unseen). Entropy-based frame selection beats random and temporal-difference selection (SR 66.70 vs 64.41 / 65.30). A supplementary orientation-prediction probe shows that without trajectory judgment the agent learns no layout knowledge (about 10% accuracy, i.e. chance among 12 bins) versus about 40% with it. Data quality and realism appear to matter more than quantity, since 587k YouTube frames slightly beat 713k Airbnb pairs.
method: Video collection and filtering: 4078 house-tour videos (433 h) sampled at 0.5 fps; Places365 ResNet and Mask R-CNN remove outdoor and person frames, leaving about 587k indoor frames.

Room-node grouping: CLIP classifies each frame's room type. Temporally adjacent frames with the same type form a room node, with random transition nodes inserted between rooms. Trajectories have K in [4,7] nodes.

Entropy-based node representation: the lowest-classification-entropy frame in a group is the node's current view, and M adjacent frames are merged to mimic a panorama. Frames are encoded as Faster R-CNN region features.

Action-aware instruction generation: 14,031 R2R-derived fill-in-blank templates; CLIP fills noun blanks with 'room with object'; a CNN action inverse model (96% accuracy) pseudo-labels go forward / turn left / turn right to fill the nearest verb blank.

Trajectory judgment pretext task: real trajectories are positives, and negatives come from shuffling transition nodes, shuffling all nodes, or inserting nodes from other videos. The dot product of [IMG] and [CLS] outputs feeds a linear layer trained with weighted BCE. It is combined with MLM, MVM and path ranking.

Backbone and adaptation: a ViLBERT-like model as in Airbert. Discriminative setting uses the path-ranking classifier with two-stage fine-tuning. Generative setting initializes DUET's language and cross-modal streams from the pre-trained model.

setting.backbone: ViLBERT-like two-stream transformer (pre-trained on YouTube-VLN, fine-tuned); DUET initialized from it for the generative setting
setting.training_data: YouTube-VLN (4078 videos, 433 h, ~587k frames, synthetic path-instruction pairs) for pre-training, then R2R/REVERIE fine-tuning; EnvDrop augmented data used in fine-tuning by default
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB features (Faster R-CNN region features) in the Matterport3D simulator; in pre-training, merged video frames
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph viewpoints (path selection among candidate paths in the discriminative setting; DUET graph node selection in the generative setting)
setting.privileged: none (the discriminative setting uses 30 candidate trajectories from EnvDrop)

results: Lily reaches 79% SR on the R2R test leaderboard in the discriminative setting (Airbert 77) and 70.00 SR on val-unseen versus Airbert's 68.67. With DUET it gains about 2-3 SR on R2R generative (val-unseen 74, test-unseen 72 versus 72 and 69). On REVERIE it beats DUET (val-unseen SR 48.11 vs 46.98, test-unseen 54.32 vs 52.51).
limitations: Restricted to graph-based discrete environments; continuous navigation trajectories are not built.
Dataset construction relies on CLIP, template-based instructions and hand-designed rules, with videos from a few YouTubers.
Gains over strong baselines are modest (about 1-3 SR), and the ablations were run without augmented data.
